questions.stem:
Relative to a fixed origin $O$,
• the point $A$ has position vector $\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}$
• the point $B$ has position vector $5\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k}$
• the point $C$ has position vector $3\mathbf{i}+p\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k}$
where $p$ is a constant.
The line $l$ passes through $A$ and $B$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find a vector equation for the line $l$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Attempts to find $\overrightarrow{AB}$. Score for subtracting either way round. Implied by 2 out of 3 correct coordinates.
M1: Attempts equation for the line, score for $\overrightarrow{OA}+\lambda\times$ their $\overrightarrow{AB}$ or $\overrightarrow{OB}+\lambda\times$ their $\overrightarrow{AB}$. No need for $r=$ for this mark.
A1: Any correct equation. Must be $r=...$ ($l=..$ is A0). e.g. $r=i-4j+3k+\lambda(4i+7j-5k)$ or $r=5i+3j-2k+\lambda(4i+7j-5k)$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Accept either vector form throughout but extra i, j k in column vectors will lose A mark in (a).
- $\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}5-1\\3--4\\-2-3\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\7\\-5\end{pmatrix}=4i+7j-5k$ M1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is perpendicular to $l$
(b) find the value of $p$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Attempts to find $\overrightarrow{AC}$. Score for subtracting either way round. Implied by 2 out of 3 correct coordinates.
M1: Takes scalar product of their $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and their $\overrightarrow{AC}$ to form and solve a linear equation in $p$
A1: $p=-8$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\overrightarrow{AC}=\begin{pmatrix}3-1\\p--4\\-1-3\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\p+4\\-4\end{pmatrix}=2i+(p+4)j-4k$ M1
- $\begin{pmatrix}2\\p+4\\-4\end{pmatrix}\bullet\begin{pmatrix}4\\7\\-5\end{pmatrix}=8+7p+28+20=0\Rightarrow p=-8$ M1A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Hence find the area of triangle $ABC$, giving your answer as a surd in simplest form.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: Attempts to find the magnitude of either their $\overrightarrow{AB}$ or their $\overrightarrow{AC}$ using their $p$
dM1: Attempts to find the exact area of the triangle $ABC$. It is dependent on the previous method mark. The most common method will be $\frac{1}{2}|\overrightarrow{AB}||\overrightarrow{AC}|$ as in scheme but other methods are possible. Such a method must be complete, including use of Pythagorean identity to find $\sin\angle ABC$. Other more advanced methods (such as cross products) are also possible.
A1: $9\sqrt{10}$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $|AB|=\sqrt{4^2+7^2+(-5)^2}=\sqrt{90}$ or $|AC|=\sqrt{2^2+(-4)^2+(-4)^2}=6$ M1
- Area $\frac{1}{2}\times"\sqrt{90}"\times"6"=9\sqrt{10}$ dM1A1
- E.g. $\cos\angle ABC=\frac{\overrightarrow{BA}.\overrightarrow{BC}}{|\overrightarrow{BA}||\overrightarrow{BC}|}\Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{2}|\overrightarrow{BA}||\overrightarrow{BC}|\sin\angle ABC$.
- If you see something you feel is worthy of some credit but does not fit the scheme, send to Review.
